A1.justification: Both 11-page PDFs describe the same DIVE work, with reliably comparable text, equations, figures and tables. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix; both refer to supplementary material that is not included.

before.justification: v1 reports original video-editing comparisons, quantitative metrics, a 50-participant preference study and qualitative ablations in Section 4.

after.justification: v2 retains original video-editing experiments and reports revised comparisons, an additional quality metric and quantitative ablations in Tables 1–2.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same three-stage pipeline: DINO feature projection for motion guidance, LoRA identity registration, and DDIM inference with background blending. The components, objectives and inference procedure are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use 30 videos from DAVIS and the Internet, eight target identity categories with DreamBench/Internet reference images, and the same image-guided and text-guided editing tasks. No additional domain or test scenario is introduced.

E2.justification: Slicedit replaces TokenFlow in both editing comparisons in Figures 4–5 and Table 1. AnyV2V, FLATTEN and RAVE remain, making this a limited comparator substitution.

E3.justification: Section 4.3 adds VBench-based Overall Video Quality, described as averaging scores across dimensions, alongside the existing CLIP metrics. Sampling, resolutions, training budgets, inference steps and the 50-participant study size remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Table 2 quantifies the existing motion-module comparison, guidance-weight sensitivity at 0, 0.3 and 1.0, and identity-guidance ablation. This supplements the retained visual analyses in Figures 6–7 without introducing new ablation conditions.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The added results retain point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: v2 adds Slicedit results, overall-quality scores and a quantitative ablation table, substantially expanding numerical evidence. DIVE's new quality scores are 0.775 for image guidance and 0.614 for text guidance; retained methods' existing CLIP scores are unchanged. DIVE preferences change from 65.08%/52.27% to 65.6%/52.8% under different comparison alternatives, so these are not direct performance gains. Figure 5 also replaces the displayed AnyV2V bear sequence.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(5), including feature projection, fusion and masked optimization objectives, are unchanged. Neither version adds formal assumptions, propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: automatic DINO-based motion correspondence and precise subject identity registration for image- or text-guided editing. The revised superiority wording does not materially change the scientific claim.

C2.justification: v2 removes the entire explicit limitations discussion from v1's Section 5. This deletes qualifications concerning identity artifacts, interactions, occlusions, large viewpoint changes, limited base-model capacity and slower per-case fine-tuning, without evidence that these limitations were resolved.

D1.justification: v2 removes the project-page link and the statement that baselines use default settings from their official repositories. Architecture, preprocessing, optimization and hardware disclosures remain unchanged. These are documentation losses, not evidence of changed implementations or unavailable resources.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to Slicedit, VBench and I2VEdit while retaining the earlier works. The positioning around DINO correspondences and avoiding VideoSwap's manual annotation remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 condenses Section 2.1, makes localized wording edits, updates affiliations and author-contact information, and adds acknowledgements. Section 5 becomes Conclusion rather than Conclusion and Limitations; the overall narrative structure remains intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 2, reformats Table 1 with an additional metric column, updates comparison panels in Figures 4–5 and revises ablation captions. The seven-figure organization and two-column layout are retained. Table 1's caption still incorrectly refers to three objective metrics.

improvement.justification: Table 2 supplies quantitative support where v1 offered visual ablations, and the added quality metric broadens validation. However, v2 removes substantive failure and efficiency limitations, baseline-setting provenance and the project link. These gains in empirical substantiation coexist with material losses in transparency and reproducibility disclosure, preventing a confident net quality judgment.
